description: Add min_samples_split=5 to the RandomForestRegressor so trees stop splitting small nodes, which regularizes tree growth.
Append each molecule's heavy atom count (mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms()) as an extra column to the Morgan fingerprint matrix in featurize.
Append each molecule's heavy atom count (mol.GetNumHeavyAtoms()) as an extra column to the Morgan fingerprint matrix in featurize.
Append Descriptors.MolWt(mol) as an extra feature column alongside the Morgan fingerprint and heavy atom count, by importing Descriptors and adding it to each featurized row.
Lower the RandomForest max_features fraction from 0.3 to 0.2 so each split considers a smaller random subset of features, decorrelating the trees.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with xgboost.XGBRegressor (n_estimators=500, max_depth=6, seeded) on the same Morgan fingerprint plus heavy-atom-count features.
Add RDKit H-bond donor (CalcNumHBD) and acceptor (CalcNumHBA) counts as two extra feature columns alongside the Morgan fingerprint and heavy atom count.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The diff changes only N_TREES from 300 to 1000. It adds no file or network access, no hard-coded answers and no use of test labels.
No bug that would make the result meaningless. More trees in a random forest only reduces variance between fits. Job time goes up about 3x, which should stay well under the 10-minute limit.

Recomputed z from the rounded numbers: (0.3979 - 0.3968) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = 0.0011 / 0.00523 ≈ 0.21. The harness gives 0.193. The gap fits the 4-decimal rounding: an unrounded difference of about 0.00101 would give 0.193. Both values are far below significance, so rejecting is correct.
Each side has only one run, so the comparison has little power. The improvement of about 0.001 is about 0.3 noise sd. If anyone wants to adopt this change, a replicate run is needed first.

description: Raise the RandomForest tree count from 300 to 1000 to reduce ensemble variance; the forest's other settings stay unchanged.

Set subsample=0.8 and colsample_bytree=0.8 on an XGBoost regressor, but train.py currently uses a RandomForestRegressor and no XGBoost model, so there is nothing to apply this to without swapping the model family.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with lightgbm.LGBMRegressor (n_estimators=500, learning_rate=0.05, seeded), keeping the same featurization.
Append RDKit physchem descriptors (Crippen logP, TPSA, rotatable bonds) to the existing Morgan fingerprint plus size/HBD/HBA features in the random forest input.
Append RDKit physchem descriptors (Crippen logP, TPSA, rotatable bonds) to the existing Morgan fingerprint plus size/HBD/HBA features in the random forest input.
Replace the RandomForestRegressor with catboost.CatBoostRegressor (iterations=1000, learning_rate=0.05, seeded, 8 threads) on the same Morgan-plus-count features.
Proposed a log10 transform of the target, but the Caco-2 values are already on a log scale, so no change is worth a slot.
Abort the "CatBoost depth" idea: the current train.py has no CatBoostRegressor to set depth=6 on, and the only CatBoost trial so far (slot 11, 0.4077) was worse than the 0.3979 incumbent.
Abort the CatBoost silent-mode idea: train.py has no CatBoostRegressor, so there is nothing to set logging_level on.
Abort the simple-mean-baseline idea: a constant mean predictor cannot beat the current Morgan+RF+HBD/HBA model (0.3979), so spending a slot on it would not change the final script.
Switch the featurize output dtype from float32 to float64 to gain numeric precision.
Add max_depth=10 to the RandomForestRegressor to cap tree depth and reduce overfitting on the small Caco-2 dataset.
Aborted the XGBoost reg_alpha/reg_lambda regularization idea: train.py has no XGBoost model to regularize, and the only XGBoost version tried (slot 5) scored 0.4770.

Append RDKit Crippen logP, TPSA, and rotatable-bond count as three extra columns alongside the existing heavy-atom, HBD and HBA features on the Morgan+RF model, re-testing the slot 9 idea on the new incumbent. The spec's name CalcRotatableBondCount does not exist in rdMolDescriptors, so the edit uses CalcNumRotatableBonds, the RDKit function that returns the same count.
CalcCrippenLogP does not exist in rdMolDescriptors; the Crippen logP function lives in rdkit.Chem.Crippen as MolLogP, so the script now imports Crippen and calls Crippen.MolLogP.
CalcCrippenLogP does not exist in rdMolDescriptors; the Crippen logP function lives in rdkit.Chem.Crippen as MolLogP, so the script now imports Crippen and calls Crippen.MolLogP.

Swap the RandomForestRegressor for sklearn's ExtraTreesRegressor, keeping the same tree count, max_features, and leaf settings, to test whether random split selection lowers variance on the Morgan+descriptor features.
Abort: moving the single featurize(train_smiles) call into a separate variable is a pure refactor with no effect on the features or predictions, so there is no loss change to test.
Abort the LightGBM feature_fraction idea: the current train.py has no LightGBM model, so the setting has nothing to apply to.
Abort the pre-compute featurization idea: it would only save runtime and cannot change the loss.
Weight each training molecule in the RandomForest fit by the inverse of its heavy atom count (a molecular-size proxy for MW), normalized to mean 1, to emphasize smaller molecules.
Weight each training molecule in the RandomForest fit by the inverse of how many training targets fall in its 10-bin histogram bin, so sparse (skewed-tail) target values get more influence.
Raise the Morgan fingerprint radius from 2 to 3 so each bit encodes a larger local chemical environment, leaving the rest of the RandomForest pipeline unchanged.
Reduce the Morgan fingerprint size from 2048 to 1024 bits (radius 2 unchanged) to test whether fewer bit collisions or a sparser feature space helps the random forest.
Switch the Morgan featurization from presence/absence bits to per-bit occurrence counts by calling GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy instead of GetFingerprintAsNumPy, leaving everything else unchanged.
Append Descriptors.MolWt(mol) and the net formal charge (Chem.GetFormalCharge) as two extra columns on the Morgan+RF feature vector.
Skip the min_samples_split=5 plus min_samples_leaf=2 regularization idea, since the same direction has already hurt the forest in two earlier slots.
Aborted the 3D-descriptor idea: the TPSA, HBD/HBA, and rotatable-bond features it names are already concatenated in featurize, and no true 3D (conformer-based) feature is in scope for a minimal edit.
Append RDKit MACCS keys (167 bits, since MACCS is a fixed-length 167-bit key set and has no 2048-bit form) to the existing Morgan fingerprint and descriptor features for the random forest.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement: MACCS keys are computed from each molecule's SMILES alone. The change doesn't read files, doesn't hard-code answers and doesn't use test labels.
No bug found: the 167-bit MACCS vector is added to the Morgan fingerprint and descriptor features in the same way for training and test molecules, so the feature matrix has the same shape for both.

Recomputed z: candidate mean is (0.3839+0.3807)/2 = 0.3823, incumbent mean is 0.3886, difference 0.0063. With noise sd 0.0037 and 2 runs on each side, SE = sqrt(0.0037²/2 + 0.0037²/2) = 0.0037, so z ≈ 1.70. This matches the harness's 1.691 up to rounding of the means.
Caveat, not a veto: the accept is borderline. It rests on only 2 runs per side and z of about 1.7, so the gain could be noise. The change is simple, though, so it fits the card's simplicity rule.

description: Append RDKit MACCS keys (167 bits, since MACCS is a fixed-length 167-bit key set and has no 2048-bit form) to the existing Morgan fingerprint and descriptor features for the random forest.
Raise the RandomForest max_features fraction from 0.3 to 1.0 so every split considers all Morgan, MACCS, and descriptor columns.
Add RDKit's aromatic ring count (CalcNumAromaticRings) as one more extra column next to the existing HBD/HBA counts, which are already in train.py.
Abort: the requested size and polarity descriptors (TPSA, HBD/HBA, rotatable bonds, heavy atom count, logP) are already in featurize(), and the remaining candidates were already rejected.

Aborted the target standard-scaling idea: for a random forest with MSE splits, standardizing y is an affine transform that leaves the tree structure and predictions unchanged, so it would only reproduce the incumbent.
Raise the Morgan fingerprint size from 2048 to 4096 bits (radius 2 unchanged) to reduce bit collisions.
Add max_samples=0.8 to the RandomForestRegressor so each tree trains on a 80% bootstrap sample, a regularization test of the Tree Pruning idea.
Apply sklearn RobustScaler to the featurized matrix before the RandomForestRegressor.
Set the RandomForest max_features fraction to 1.0 and raise the tree count to 1000 so each split sees all features with more trees for variance reduction.
Set LightGBM num_leaves=31 and num_threads=8 for the LightGBM model.

Abort: the proposed min_samples_split=5 plus min_samples_leaf=2 regularization repeats a direction already tested and rejected (slot 0 min_samples_split=5 scored 0.4546, +0.0129), and other tree-capping regularizers (max_depth=10, 0.4078) also hurt.
Replace the single RandomForestRegressor with the median of five forests trained on different seeds to reduce variance.

Abort: the proposed change sets n_estimators=1000 on an XGBoost model, but the current train.py contains no XGBoost model; it uses a RandomForestRegressor whose tree count was already tested (slot 7, 1000 trees, -0.0010, within noise).
Aborted the RobustScaler idea: a per-column affine scaling leaves RandomForest splits unchanged, so the job would reproduce the incumbent and waste a slot.

Abort the target-scaling idea: a StandardScaler or MinMaxScaler on y is an affine map, and RandomForest MSE splits are invariant to it, so predictions would be unchanged apart from floating-point noise.
Abort the max_features=1.0 idea because the same change was already tested at slot 27 and rejected (0.3908 against the 0.3823 incumbent).
Abort the 1024-bit Morgan idea: reducing N_BITS from 2048 to 1024 was already tested at slot 22 and rejected (0.3976 against the then-incumbent), so this would repeat a known result.
Abort the CatBoost swap: the same model replacement was already tested at slot 11 (0.4077, rejected), and the notes say model swaps have not helped, so it is not worth another slot.
Abort the LightGBM swap: it repeats slot 8, which already tested LGBMRegressor and was rejected (0.4244, +0.0266 vs incumbent), and the notes say model swaps have not helped.

issues: None blocking. The diff only swaps RandomForestRegressor for ExtraTreesRegressor and keeps the same hyperparameters, all of which ExtraTreesRegressor accepts. It reads no files, pastes no answers, uses no test labels and keeps the seed for randomness.

z recomputed as (0.3823 - 0.3853) / (0.0037 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/2)) = -0.662. The harness gives -0.668. The small gap is probably because the shown means are rounded. The candidate is about 0.003 worse, which is under 1 sd and not significant. Rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.
Only one candidate run was made, so this comparison is weak. That does not justify a veto.

Abort the "Add MACCS Keys" idea because the current train.py already concatenates MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys(mol) to the Morgan and descriptor features, so the proposed change would be a no-op.

Abort: swapping the RandomForestRegressor for xgboost.XGBRegressor was already tested at slot 5 (n_estimators=500, max_depth 6 settings), scoring 0.4770, far worse than the incumbent, so this spec would repeat a known loser.
Train five RandomForestRegressor models with seeds seed..seed+4 on the same features and return the element-wise median of their test predictions, to reduce seed variance.

Add the three principal moments of inertia (CalcPMI1/2/3) as extra shape columns, computed after a fixed-seed ETKDG 3D embedding of each molecule (PMI needs coordinates, so the "conformer-independent" label in the spec does not hold), with zeros if embedding fails.
